# Maximum Score After Splitting a String.

@example The cuts after 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 characters score 2, 3, 4, 3 and 4.
"100101"
=> 4

@example The back piece must keep a 0, so only two of the three 0s can score.
"000"
=> 2

@example The only cut leaves the 1 in front and the 0 at the back, which scores nothing.
"10"
=> 0

# The other strings of length 2.
"00"
=> 1

"01"
=> 2

"11"
=> 1

# All 1s: the front piece must take one of them.
"11111"
=> 4

# The best cut is right after the first character.
"01101"
=> 4

# The best cut is right before the last character.
"10001"
=> 4

# A lone 1 at the front; a lone 0 at the end.
"10000"
=> 3

"11110"
=> 3

# Alternating: three cuts tie for the best.
"0101010"
=> 4

# 250 0s then 250 1s: the middle cut scores all 500 characters, more than
# a byte-sized counter holds.
""
=> 500

# 500 1s, and 500 0s: every character but one scores.
""
=> 499

""
=> 499

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 2 small
"000010"
=> 5

@gen 3 small
"11100001"
=> 5

@gen 6 small
"1110000"
=> 3

@gen 8 small
"00000111"
=> 8

@gen 12 small
"100"
=> 1

@gen 15 small
"1001111"
=> 6

# Full-size random cases.
@gen 1
""
=> 250

@gen 2
""
=> 440

@gen 3
""
=> 272
